title: Unsupervised Learning: K-Means
status: Draft practice quiz; teacher review required
instructions: Ten questions. Select all correct options in multiple-choice items. One point for an exact match.

questions.prompt: A dataset contains six 2D points but no class labels. You want to group nearby points. Which algorithm fits best?
questions.explanation: K-Means groups unlabelled observations into clusters.

questions.prompt: What does K mean in K-Means?
questions.explanation: K is the chosen number of cluster centres.

questions.prompt: A cluster contains (1,1), (2,1), (3,1). What is its centroid?
What usually happens after a K-Means algorithm assigns every point to its nearest centre?
options: Update each centre to the mean of assigned points
questions.explanation: The update step calculates new centroids from assigned points.

questions.prompt: Two points have coordinates (0,0) and (3,4). Their Euclidean distance is:
An algorithm starts with different random centres and ends with different groupings. What does this illustrate?
options: K-Means can be sensitive to its initial centres
K-Means always gives the true labels
questions.explanation: Initialisation can affect convergence and the final grouping.

questions.prompt: A new point is placed at the same coordinates as an existing cluster centre. Which centre is nearest?
options: Always the centre with the largest index
The centre that has the most labels

questions.prompt: Why should K-Means cluster IDs not be treated automatically as the real class labels?
options: Clusters are discovered without known target labels
Every dataset has exactly two classes
questions.explanation: Clustering identifies geometric groups; their meaning requires separate interpretation.

questions.prompt: Select ALL statements that describe ordinary K-Means.
options: It repeatedly assigns points and updates centroids
It needs a chosen number K of clusters
It always uses provided yes/no target labels
It guarantees a global optimum for every initialisation
questions.explanation: K-Means alternates assignments and centroid updates; it is unsupervised and sensitive to initial conditions.

questions.prompt: Select ALL useful checks when presenting a cluster analysis.
options: Plot the points and the selected centres
Compare the result when K or initial centres change
Assume two clusters prove two real-world categories exist
Ignore the distance units of the features
questions.explanation: Visual inspection and sensitivity checks help interpret the grouping without overclaiming meaning.
